best_for: Windows users who want the open-source Chromium browser built with video codecs and sync working, without Google Chrome's own branding and services.

points.title: A community build, not Google's
points.text: These builds come from Hibbiki's GitHub project, chromium-win64, which compiles the open-source Chromium code for Windows. It is not a Google release and carries no Google support.

points.title: Codecs and sync switched on
points.text: The README says H.264, HEVC and other licensed codecs are enabled, Widevine is included for protected video, and sign-in sync works with Google API keys. Field trials, Chrome's server-pushed experiments, are turned off.

points.title: Updates are on you
points.text: The README describes no auto-updater. New builds appear on the GitHub releases page; ten came out between 10 October and 19 November, so plan to check back.

points.title: What each release contains
points.text: A release carries `mini_installer.exe`, a `chrome.7z` archive you can unpack and run without installing, and a zip of policy templates for admins who manage settings by Group Policy.

points.title: Windows x64 only
points.text: There are no Arm64, 32-bit, Mac or Linux builds in this project. The installers listed here cover x64, for the current user or the whole machine.

points.title: A long history to roll back to
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 185 versions, which helps when a site or extension breaks on a new Chromium release and you need the build before it.
